Fixes #861

The original motivation behind this is to make it work with Firefox. But it also helped make the code more intentional.

Test Plan:
- Create one square, select it, zoom in repeatedly, make sure that it zooms centered in the screen and everything looks good
- Scroll at various zoom levels, things look good
- Export a small scene at 1x and 3x, make sure the background is properly set and look good

@marcomilanesio that's a year old Firefox (with a usage of 0.05%, we officially support >0.2% usage). If you can update to latest, this should be resovled.

There's still two cases of `getTransform` in `zoom.ts`:

https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/blob/e1e2249f577d73229902ad23ad76b2c880a39350/src/scene/zoom.ts#L10-L11

Also, AFAIK `setTransform` still affects Firefox Mobile:

https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/blob/e1e2249f577d73229902ad23ad76b2c880a39350/src/components/App.tsx#L804

But that one should be simple to fix.
Oops, I should have grepped the entire codebase. Both of them should be easy to fix.

review_comments: This was mostly used for getting the pixel ratio of the device. The canvas is scaled outside of this function. Now we pass it as argument
The initial translate got reset via context.reset, which is not the most expected behavior
We probably don't need to do the scroll translate twice, but this diff is big enough that I didn't want to touch it
I have no idea why we did all this hackery. I don't think it's needed
I removed all the instances of context.save() in favor of explicit set and restore of all the properties
This is a very convoluted way to do context.translate() and context.scale()
This was needlessly applying and resetting around each section. We only need to apply and restore once
